title: The megafires of California
subject: reading

paragraphs.text: Drought, housing expansion, and oversupply of tinder make for
bigger, hotter Gies in the western United States

Wildfires are becoming an increasing menace in the western United States, with Southern California being the hardest hit area. There's a reason fire squads battling more frequent blazes in Southern California are having such difficulty containing the flames, despite better preparedness than ever and decades of experience fighting fires fanned by the 'Santa Ana Winds'. The wildfires themselves, experts say, are generally hotter, faster, and spread more erratically than in the past.

Megafires, also called 'siege fires', are the increasingly frequent blazes that burn 500,000 acres or more - 10 times the size of the average forest fire of 20 years ago. Some recent wildfires are among the biggest ever in California in terms of acreage burned, according to state figures and news reports.

One explanation for the trend to more superhot fires is that the region, which usually has dry summers, has had significantly below normal precipitation in many recent years. Another reason, experts say, is related to the century? long policy of the US Forest Service to stop wildfires as quickly as possible.The unintentional consequence has been to halt the natural eradication of underbrush, now the primary fuel for megafires.

Three other factors contribute to the trend, they add. First is climate change, marked by a 1-degree Fahrenheit rise in average yearly temperature across the western states. Second is fire seasons that on average are 78 days longer than they were 20 years ago. Third is increased construction of homes in wooded areas.

'We are increasingly building our homes in fire-prone ecosystems,' 1 says Dominik Kulakowski, adjunct professor of biology at Clark University Graduate School of Geography in Worcester, Massachusetts. 1 Doing that in many of the forests of the western US is like building homes on the side of an active volcano.’

In California, where population growth has averaged more than 600,000 a year for at least a decade, more residential housing is being built.'What once was open space is now residential homes providing fuel to make fires burn with greater intensity,' says Terry McHale of the California Department of Forestry firefighters'union. 'With so much dryness, so many communities to catch fire, so many fronts to fight, it becomes an almost incredible job.'

That said, many experts give California high marks for making progress on preparedness in recent years, after some of the largest fires in state history scorched thousands of acres, burned thousands of homes, and killed numerous people. Stung in the past by criticism of bungling that allowed fires to spread when they might have been contained, personnel are meeting the peculiar challenges of neighborhood - and canyon- hopping fires better than previously, observers say.

State promises to provide more up-to-date engines, planes, and helicopters to fight fires have been fulfilled. Firefighters' unions that in the past complained of dilapidated equipment, old fire engines, and insufficient blueprints for fire safety are now praising the state's commitment, noting that funding for firefighting has increased, despite huge cuts in many other programs. ' We are pleased that the current state administration has been very proactive in its support of us, and [has]come through with budgetary support of the infrastructure needs we have long sought,' says Mr. McHale of the firefighters' union.

Besides providing money to upgrade the fire engines that must traverse the mammoth state and wind along serpentine canyon roads, the state has invested in better command-and-control facilities as well as in the strategies to run them.' In the fire sieges of earlier years, we found that other jurisdictions and states were willing to offer mutual-aid help, but we were not able to communicate adequately with them/ says Kim Zagaris, chief of the state's Office of Emergency Services Fire and Rescue Branch.After a commission examined and revamped communications procedures, the statewide response' has become far more professional and responsive/ he says. There is a sense among both government officials and residents that the speed, dedication, and coordination of firefighters from several states and jurisdictions are resulting in greater efficiency than in past 'siege fire' situations.

In recent years, the Southern California region has improved building codes, evacuation procedures, and procurement of new technology. ' I am extraordinarily impressed by the improvements we have witnessed,' says Randy Jacobs, a Southern Californiabased lawyer who has had to evacuate both his home and business to escape wildfires.' Notwithstanding all the damage that will continue to be caused by wildfires, we will no longer suffer the loss of life endured in the past because of the fire prevention and firefighting measures that have been put in place,' he says.

questions.explanation:
题号：1

定位词：movement, more unpredictably

第一段最后一句：The wildfires themselves, experts say, are generally hotter, faster, and spread more erratically than in the past.解答笔记填空题时，除了阅读空格所在句之外，考生最好也能整体性地快速通读一下整体内容，这样往往能够获得额外提示。比如在做本题时，如果考生只关注空格前后的movement和unpredictably,则一定需要认识原文中erratically这个同义替换词才能顺利定位；而如果通读了整体内容则可知，第1题和第2题都需要寻找描述“现在的野火与过去相比所具有的特征属性"的相关内容,且还有用以举例的几个特点more frequent, hotter 和faster,则可以更加顺利地定位并规避生词难度顺利解题，答案为spread。

题号：2

定位词：size, two，decades ago

第二段最后一句：Megafires, also called 'siege fires'，are the increasingly frequent blazes that burn 500,000 acres or more- -10 times the size of the average forest fire of 20 years ago.原文中出现了size这个题干词的原词重现和20这个明显数字定位词，定位十分容易，整个句子结构也不难理解，答案为10 times。

题号：3

定位词：rainfall, average

第三段最后一句：One explanation for the trend to more superhot fires is that the region, which usually has dry summers, has had significantly below normal precipitation in many recent years.此题的同义替换难度比较高，原文中用了precipitation这个不太常见的词替换了题干中的rainfall,而题干中的average也被替换成了normal。不过如前所说，如果对整体题干通读后，则可知此题的定位应当在后面第4题brush之前，也就是答案必定在one explanation这个句子之中。通过分析原文，考生依然有希望在不认识precipitation的情况下顺利解题，答案为below。

题号：4

定位词：brush, act as

第三段最后一句：The unintentional consequence has been to halt the natural eradication of underbrush, now the primary fuel for megafires. 本题的定位不困难，只需读懂定位句子的大致结构和意思即可得出答案为fuel。

题号：5

定位词：extended fire

第四段第三句：Second is fire seasons that on average are 78 days longer than they were 20 years ago.解答此题只需考生认识到extended一词与longer than形成了简单同义替换关系即可，答案为seasons。

题号：6

定位词：More building of

第四段最后一句：Third is increased construction of homes in wooded areas.词题难度也不高，使用了construction与building两词的同意替换，答案为homes。

groups.contextHtml:
Wildfires

• Characteristics of wildfires and wildfire conditions today compared to the past:

- occurrence: more frequent

- temperature: hotter

- speed: faster

- movement:[1] ______more unpredictably

- size of fires: [2] ______greater on average than two decades ago

• Reasons wildfires cause more damage today compared to the past:

-rainfall: [3] ______average

- more brush to act as [4] ______

- increase in yearly temperature

- extended fire[5] ______

- more building of [6] ______in vulnerable places

groups.instruction:
Questions 7-13

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?

Choose TRUE if the statement agrees with the information,

choose FALSE if the statement contradicts the information,

or choose NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.

questions.prompt: The amount of open space in California has diminished over the last ten years.
questions.explanation:
译文：加州的空地在过去十年里减少了。

定位词：open space, diminished, last ten years

In California, where population growth has averaged more than600,000 a year for at least a

decade, more residential housing is being built. What once was open space is now residential homes providing fuel to make fires burn with greater intensity,' says Terry McHale of the California Department of Forestry firefighters' union.

此题的定位有个小小的难点，若是考生只关注open space这个定位词组，则它所在的句子并未提及“过去十年”这样一条解题时同样需要考虑的信息。此处两句原文之间的关系是：过去十年来人口增长导致需要建立更多住房，而住房所需用地又占用了以前是空地的区域，综合两句可知答案为TRUE。

questions.prompt: Many experts believe California has made little progress in readying itself to fight fires.
questions.explanation:
译文：许多专家相信，加州在做好准备应对火灾方面没有做出什么进步。

定位词：experts, little, progress, readying

That said, many experts give California high marks for making progress on preparedness in recent years...killed numerous people.

本句的详细解析请见前文“佳句赏析”，原文内容是许多专家给加州事前准备工作的进步打出了高分，也就是认可其做出的改进，与选项内容相矛盾，答案为FALSE。

questions.prompt: Personnel in the past have been criticised for mishandling fire containment.
questions.explanation:
译文：救火人员在过去曾被指责对火灾控制工作处理不当。

定位词：Personnel, criticised for mishandling

Stung in the past by criticism of bungling that allowed fires to spread when they might have been contained, personnel are meeting the peculiar challenges of neighborhood- -and canyon-hopping fires better than previously, observers say.

本题的难度之一在于句子很长且有难度，可能会让一部分考生感到费解;之二在于criticism和bungling这两个贬义词认识至少一个，才能更方便地理解文意，否则只好根据句子内部的逻辑关系推导其意思了。救火人员在过去确实遭到了批评，原因也确实为控制火势不当，与题干内容相符，答案为TRUE。

questions.prompt: California has replaced a range of firefighting tools
questions.explanation:
译文：加州已经置换了一批救火工具。

定位词：replaced, fire fighting tools

第八段首句：State promises to provide more up-to-date engines, planes, and helicopters to fight fires have been fulfilled,第九段首句：Besides providing money to, upgrade the fire engines ...to run them

本题对考生理解同义替换词的能力要求略高。原文中两次提及“政府承诺提供更新的救火设备并已兑现了诺言”(第八段首句)，以及“提供资金以升级换代救火机车" (第九段首句)，考生需要做的就是灵活理解题干中replace与原文中的up to date和upgrade皆为表达类似意思的同义替换即可。至于更新的对象，则原文中的机车、飞机和直升机皆为救火工具的具体内容，答案为TRUE。

questions.prompt: More firefighters have been hired to improve fire-fighting capacity.
questions.explanation:
译文：雇用了更多的消防队员以增加抗火救灾能力。

定位词：More firefighters, improve, fire-fighting capacity

原文中只是提到了设备的更新换代和资金投入的增加,并未提及任何“消防人员"的相关信息，答案为NOT GIVEN。

questions.prompt: Citizens and government groups disapprove of the efforts of different states and agencies working together.
questions.explanation:
译文：普通公民和政府成员并不费成不同的州和组织一起协同合作。

定位词：Citizens and government groups, disapprove, working together

第九段最后一句There is a sense among both government officials and residents that the speed, dedication, and coordination of firefighters from several states and jurisdictions are resulting in greater efficiency than in past 'siege fire' situations.

本句的详细解释请见前文“佳句赏析”。原文说政府和居民都感觉到各团体和州政府合作以后效率提高了，显然对此种做法抱赞同态度，与题干内容相矛盾抵触，答案为FALSE。

questions.prompt: Randy Jacobs believes that loss of life from fires will continue at the same levels, despite changes made.
questions.explanation:
译文: Randy Jacobs相信，虽然做出了一些改变，但由火灾造成的生命损失还是会保持同样的水平。

定位词：Randy Jacobs

第十段第二句至最后一句：I am extraordinarily impressed by the improvements we have witnessed," says Randy, Jacobs, .... we will no longer suffer the loss of life endured in the past...

原文明确说到这位律师的看法是：虽然火灾造成的破坏在所难免，但他们不会再遭受之前那样的生命损失了，与题干内容相矛盾，答案为FALSE。

articleHtml:
The megafires of California
Drought, housing expansion, and oversupply of tinder make for
bigger, hotter Gies in the western United States

Wildfires are becoming an increasing menace in the western United States, with Southern California being the hardest hit area. There's a reason fire squads battling more frequent blazes in Southern California are having such difficulty containing the flames, despite better preparedness than ever and decades of experience fighting fires fanned by the 'Santa Ana Winds'. The wildfires themselves, experts say, are generally hotter, faster, and spread more erratically than in the past.

Megafires, also called 'siege fires', are the increasingly frequent blazes that burn 500,000 acres or more - 10 times the size of the average forest fire of 20 years ago. Some recent wildfires are among the biggest ever in California in terms of acreage burned, according to state figures and news reports.

One explanation for the trend to more superhot fires is that the region, which usually has dry summers, has had significantly below normal precipitation in many recent years. Another reason, experts say, is related to the century? long policy of the US Forest Service to stop wildfires as quickly as possible.The unintentional consequence has been to halt the natural eradication of underbrush, now the primary fuel for megafires.

Three other factors contribute to the trend, they add. First is climate change, marked by a 1-degree Fahrenheit rise in average yearly temperature across the western states. Second is fire seasons that on average are 78 days longer than they were 20 years ago. Third is increased construction of homes in wooded areas.

'We are increasingly building our homes in fire-prone ecosystems,' 1 says Dominik Kulakowski, adjunct professor of biology at Clark University Graduate School of Geography in Worcester, Massachusetts. 1 Doing that in many of the forests of the western US is like building homes on the side of an active volcano.’

In California, where population growth has averaged more than 600,000 a year for at least a decade, more residential housing is being built.'What once was open space is now residential homes providing fuel to make fires burn with greater intensity,' says Terry McHale of the California Department of Forestry firefighters'union. 'With so much dryness, so many communities to catch fire, so many fronts to fight, it becomes an almost incredible job.'

That said, many experts give California high marks for making progress on preparedness in recent years, after some of the largest fires in state history scorched thousands of acres, burned thousands of homes, and killed numerous people. Stung in the past by criticism of bungling that allowed fires to spread when they might have been contained, personnel are meeting the peculiar challenges of neighborhood - and canyon- hopping fires better than previously, observers say.

State promises to provide more up-to-date engines, planes, and helicopters to fight fires have been fulfilled. Firefighters' unions that in the past complained of dilapidated equipment, old fire engines, and insufficient blueprints for fire safety are now praising the state's commitment, noting that funding for firefighting has increased, despite huge cuts in many other programs. ' We are pleased that the current state administration has been very proactive in its support of us, and [has]come through with budgetary support of the infrastructure needs we have long sought,' says Mr. McHale of the firefighters' union.

Besides providing money to upgrade the fire engines that must traverse the mammoth state and wind along serpentine canyon roads, the state has invested in better command-and-control facilities as well as in the strategies to run them.' In the fire sieges of earlier years, we found that other jurisdictions and states were willing to offer mutual-aid help, but we were not able to communicate adequately with them/ says Kim Zagaris, chief of the state's Office of Emergency Services Fire and Rescue Branch.After a commission examined and revamped communications procedures, the statewide response' has become far more professional and responsive/ he says. There is a sense among both government officials and residents that the speed, dedication, and coordination of firefighters from several states and jurisdictions are resulting in greater efficiency than in past 'siege fire' situations.

In recent years, the Southern California region has improved building codes, evacuation procedures, and procurement of new technology. ' I am extraordinarily impressed by the improvements we have witnessed,' says Randy Jacobs, a Southern Californiabased lawyer who has had to evacuate both his home and business to escape wildfires.' Notwithstanding all the damage that will continue to be caused by wildfires, we will no longer suffer the loss of life endured in the past because of the fire prevention and firefighting measures that have been put in place,' he says.
